stemMd: Under the designers’ approach, when could colour variation be acceptable?

options.label: A
options.textMd: When the catalogue conceals it until installation.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Only when no customer can notice it.

options.label: C
options.textMd: When it is disclosed and the tiles still meet required functional standards.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Whenever recycled material is used, regardless of performance.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Only if all strength tests are omitted.

explanationMd: The designers distinguish appearance from minimum functional requirements. They allow visual variation as a chosen feature if buyers are informed, while still requiring strength and absorption standards. Neither concealment nor blanket exemption is supported.

distractorRationale.d: The passage explicitly rejects excusing poor performance.
distractorRationale.b: The designers propose treating visible variation as an intended feature.
distractorRationale.e: Testing remains part of the approach.
distractorRationale.a: Advance disclosure is central to the argument.
